boilerplate.section_intro: This section consists of questions and problems involving quantitative reasoning.  Each question is followed by four possible responses.  Choose the correct answer and mark its number in the appropriate place on the answer sheet.

boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro:
Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

A certain radio station publishes every week a chart in which the 20 most-loved songs of that week are ranked (in first place is the most-loved song, and so forth).  The graph presents the rankings of all the songs of four singers – Orly, Bat-Chen, Galit and Dorin – starting from week 1 of a certain year and up to week 20 of it.  Songs of additional singers were ranked in the chart, but these are not presented in the graph.
Every line in the graph represents one song of one singer (see key).  The emphasized points on the line represent the ranking of this song in the weeks in which it participated in the chart.  In the week in which a song entered the chart, a circle appears around its point indicating the style of the song: pop, rock, Mediterranean or hip hop (see key).

For example: In week 6 a pop song of Galit entered the chart and was ranked in 2nd place.  Week 14 was the last week in which this song was ranked in the chart.

Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow.

The graph describes flight routes between five countries: England, Belgium, Germany, Denmark and Holland.
Every arrow describes a direct flight between two countries.  The arrow leaves the country from which the plane takes off and points to the country in which the plane lands.
It is possible to get from one country to another not necessarily on one direct flight, but also if there is a route of several flights connecting the two countries.

For example: there is no direct flight from Holland to Germany, but it is possible to get from Holland to Germany on a route on which there are two direct flights: a direct flight from Holland to Denmark and a direct flight from Denmark to Germany.

questions.stem:
In the coordinate system in the accompanying figure there are two congruent triangles.  The sides AB and CD are parallel to the x-axis.

Based on this information and the information in the figure, what are the values of point A?
Which of the following expressions is equal to \(27^3\)?

methods.text: A power of a power multiplies the exponents. Option (1) is what adding them would give in spirit, and it is the standard wrong answer.

questions.stem: Given: a < 2b b < 5 Which of the following inequalities is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(b<5\) gives \(2b<10\), and \(a<2b\), so \(a<10\) by chaining.
Nothing else is forced. \(a\) can exceed \(b\), exceed 5 and exceed 3 all at once — take \(b=4.9\) and \(a=9\), which satisfies both givens and kills (2), (3) and (4) together.

questions.stem:
Based on the information in the figure,
by how much is the area of the light triangle greater than the area of the dark triangle?
How many different five-digit numbers is it possible to create from the digits 2, 5, 5, 7, 7 so that the first digit in the number and the last digit in the number will be the same digits?

Shmuel had a stamp collection.  He wanted to divide the stamps in the collection equally between his two sons.  Afterwards he changed his mind and thought to divide the stamps equally between his five grandchildren.  In the end he decided to divide the stamps equally between all his sons and grandchildren.  Each one of the above divisions is possible to carry out without a remainder.

What is the smallest possible number of stamps in Shmuel's collection?

methods.text: The total must be divisible by 2, by 5 and by 7 (two sons, five grandchildren, then all seven). So it is divisible by their LCM.
\(2\), \(5\) and \(7\) are pairwise coprime, so the LCM is simply their product, 70. That is the smallest total that works.

questions.stem:
In the zoo there are three gorillas.  Their average weight is 135 kg.

What does the weight of a fourth gorilla need to be so that the average weight of the four of them will be 120 kg?

In a certain nature reserve there are 25 species of flowers.
\(\frac{4}{5}\) of the species of flowers are protected species.  \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the species of flowers are species whose colour is purple.

It is possible that in the nature reserve there are ______ protected species of flowers whose colour is purple.
In which weeks did Bat-Chen have 3 songs in the chart at the same time?

A "strong singer" is a singer each of whose songs was ranked in one of the three first places in the week in which it entered the chart.

Which of the four singers is a strong singer?
How many of the rock songs appearing in the graph rose in ranking in the chart at some stage, and at a later stage fell in ranking?

It is known that in one of the first 10 weeks a song that does not appear in the graph was ranked in first place.  A week later this song was ranked in place x, and one more week later it was ranked again in first place.

Which of the following numbers can be equal to x?

Shimon rolls a wheel whose radius is \(\frac{1}{4}\) meter at a constant speed.
The wheel rolls 4 complete rotations in 12 seconds.

How many meters did the wheel travel in one second?

In the first year of its life a tree sprouted and grew to a height of one meter.  In every remaining year of its life the height of the tree grew by half of the height that was added to it in the preceding year.

What was the height of the tree (in meters) at the end of the fourth year of its life?

A certain calculator is able to perform two calculation operations only: raising a number to the power of two, and calculating a square root. Let us enter into the calculator a certain positive integer, and the calculator performs on it one of the calculation operations. On the result that was obtained it performs the other calculation operation. Which of the following numbers cannot be the final result obtained in the calculator?

Given:  a is 75% of b.
b is x% of c.

Which of the following expressions is equal to a?

Given:  y is a certain integer.
\(x = y + \sqrt{2}\)

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
Given: 2x + y = 60 x + 2y = 30 Which of the following equations is not true?

methods.text: Adding gives \(3x+3y = 90\), so \(x+y = 30\); subtracting gives \(x - y = 30\). Together \(x = 30\) and \(y = 0\). Then \(4x + 2y = 120\), not 60.
Once \(x=30, y=0\) is known, each option is one substitution. Options (1), (2) and (3) all come out true, and (4) does not.

The accompanying figure shows a circle whose center is O, in which are inscribed the square ABCD and the regular hexagon EBFGDH.

\(\alpha\) = ?

The accompanying figure shows a triangular prism.  Its lateral faces are squares the area of each one of which is \(\sqrt{3}\) cm².

The area of the base of the prism (the dark triangle) is ______ cm².

Sachar and Roni are standing on the perimeter of the square drawn on the lot.  The length of the side of the square is 5 meters.

What is the greatest distance that can be between Sachar and Roni (in a straight line)?

Ohad and Ronena are parking inspectors.  On the first day Ohad inspected x cars per hour, whereas Ronena inspected y cars per hour  (0 < x , y).  On the second day Ohad increased his work rate by a factor of 2 and Ronena increased her work rate by a factor of 3.
The number of daily work hours of Ohad is fixed and is identical to the number of daily work hours of Ronena.

By how much is the total number of cars that they inspected on the second day greater than the total number of cars that they inspected on the first day?

methods.text: Day one they do \(x + y\) an hour; day two \(2x + 3y\). The ratio of the two days' output is \(\frac{2x+3y}{x+y}\).
Different multipliers on the two workers means the combined rate does not scale by any single factor — which is why the answer has to stay as a fraction.

questions.stem:
Eli had 4 candies more than Shlomit.

Which of the following statements is necessarily true?
options: After Eli gave Shlomit 4 candies, the numbers of candies of the two of them were equal
After Eli gave Shlomit 3 candies, the difference between the numbers of candies of the two of them grew
After Shlomit gave Eli 2 candies, the difference between the numbers of candies of the two of them decreased
After Eli gave Shlomit one candy, the difference between the numbers of candies of the two of them decreased

questions.stem:
Given:  \(t^2 = w^2\)
\(t \neq w\)
M is the average of t and w.

Which of the following statements is necessarily true regarding M?
options: It is greater than the difference between t and w
It is equal to the difference between t and w

methods.text: \(t^2=w^2\) means the two have the same size, and \(t\ne w\) rules out their being identical — so they are opposites. The average of a number and its opposite is 0.
\(t^2-w^2=0\) factors as \((t-w)(t+w)=0\). Since \(t\ne w\) the first factor is non-zero, so \(t+w=0\) and \(M=\frac{t+w}2=0\).

questions.stem:
A is a point on the perimeter of a circle whose center is O.
Given:  OAB is a right-angled triangle, and its area is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) cm².

Based on this information and the information in the figure,
what is the area of the dark sector (in cm²)?

x is an integer that is divisible by 3.

If it is known that \(\sqrt{x}\) is an integer, how many possible values are there for x between 1 and 100?

methods.text: \(\sqrt x\) whole means \(x\) is a perfect square; divisible by 3 then forces \(x\) to be divisible by \(3^2 = 9\), since a prime in a square appears an even number of times.
So \(x\) is a square multiple of 9 below 100: \(9, 36, 81\) — three of them. The trap is counting multiples of 3 that are squares without realising 9 is forced.

questions.stem: Given: x and y are negative integers. z is an even number. \((y \cdot x^2 \cdot z)\) is necessarily –

methods.text: \(z\) is even, and anything multiplied by an even number is even. The signs of \(x\) and \(y\) are irrelevant to parity, so the product is necessarily even.
The sign is not fixed, which kills (1) and (2): \(z\) is only said to be even, so it may be positive or negative, and \(y \cdot x^2\) is negative. Take \(z = 2\) and \(z = -2\) to get opposite signs.

questions.stem:
Two countries are a "mutually connected pair" if it is possible to get from each one of them to the other on one direct flight.

How many mutually connected pairs are there in the graph?

A country is called "central" if it is possible to get from it (not necessarily on a direct flight) to every other country.

How many central countries are there?
What is the greatest number of direct flights that it is possible to fly one after the other without passing twice through the same country?

Adna spent time in Holland and planned to fly on a direct flight to another country but mistakenly boarded the wrong flight. In order to correct her mistake and get to the country to which she had planned to fly, Adna needed two additional flights. To which country did Adna plan to fly?

In a certain orchestra the number of violin players is one third of the number of players of string instruments and one fifth of the number of players of the whole orchestra.

Therefore, the number of players of string instruments is ______ of the number of players of the whole orchestra.

methods.text: Violins are \(\frac13\) of strings and \(\frac15\) of the orchestra, so strings are \(3 \times \frac15 = \frac35\) of the orchestra — 60%.
Take 15 players: 3 violins, so 9 strings, and \(\frac{9}{15} = 60\%\) ✓.

AF = AC

Based on this information and the information in the figure,

a and b are positive numbers.

\(\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{b}{a} + \dfrac{a}{b} + 2\right) \cdot \dfrac{1}{ab}}\) = ?

methods.text: The bracket is \(\dfrac{a^2+b^2+2ab}{ab} = \dfrac{(a+b)^2}{ab}\). Multiplying by \(\frac{1}{ab}\) gives \(\dfrac{(a+b)^2}{a^2b^2}\), whose square root is \(\dfrac{a+b}{ab} = \dfrac1a + \dfrac1b\).
\(a=1, b=1\): the stem is \(\sqrt{4} = 2\), and \(\frac11+\frac11 = 2\). Option (4) also gives 2, so test \(a=1, b=2\): the stem is \(\sqrt{4.5/2} = 1.5\), matching \(1+0.5\) and not 3.
The \(+2\) inside the bracket is the giveaway — it is the \(2ab\) that completes the square.

questions.stem:
During the screening of a film more than \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the viewers left the cinema hall, and no viewer entered.
At the end of the film there were 22 viewers in the hall.

At the start of the screening the number of viewers in the hall was at least –
x and y are numbers different from 0. Given: \(|x + y| = |x| - |y|\) Which of the following inequalities is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(|x|-|y|\) is smaller than \(|x|+|y|\), so the given says the sum cancels rather than accumulates — which happens exactly when \(x\) and \(y\) have opposite signs. That makes the product negative.
The right side must be non-negative, so \(|x|\ge|y|\). Squaring gives \(x^2+2xy+y^2=x^2-2|xy|+y^2\), so \(2xy=-2|xy|\), which forces \(xy\le0\) — and \(xy\ne0\) since neither is zero.
\(x=5,\ y=-2\) satisfies the given (\(3=5-2\)) with a positive sum; \(x=-5,\ y=2\) satisfies it with a negative sum. So (2) fails, and swapping the sizes kills (3) and (4).
